boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named destinations along distinct Fullerton corridors, each paired with one source-backed reason to leave campus.

cards.title: Take the Recreation Trail
cards.subtitle: Fullerton Creek Drive — recreation trail
cards.notes: Follow Fullerton Creek Drive to Acacia Park, then use its recreation trail for a walk away from campus routines.
cards.short_summary: A tree-filled park block with a designated recreation trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fullerton lists Acacia Park at 1910 Fullerton Creek Drive and identifies recreation trails among its amenities.
cards.source_title: Acacia Park | List of Parks | Fullerton, CA
cards.access_notes: Use posted park rules and conditions; the official page does not state operating hours.

cards.title: Find a Court and a Picnic Shelter
cards.subtitle: San Carlos Drive — basketball and sheltered tables
cards.notes: Turn onto San Carlos Drive for Chapman Park; bring a ball or lunch and use the listed court or picnic shelter.
cards.short_summary: A recreation stop combining basketball with sheltered picnic space.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Fullerton places Chapman Park at 2515 San Carlos Drive and lists basketball and a picnic shelter among its amenities.
cards.source_title: Chapman Park | List of Parks | Fullerton, CA
cards.access_notes: Use posted park rules; availability may vary around organized recreation programs.

cards.title: Join the Lost Trail
cards.subtitle: Silver Pine Street — trail access
cards.notes: Take Silver Pine Street to the sports complex and use its documented connection to the Lost Trail beyond the fields.
cards.short_summary: A sports-focused block that doubles as an entry to the Lost Trail.
cards.evidence_claim: The City identifies 560 E. Silver Pine Street as the Fullerton Sports Complex and says it provides access to the Lost Trail.
cards.source_title: Fullerton Sports Complex | List of Parks | Fullerton, CA
cards.access_notes: Use designated park and trail areas; the official page does not provide operating hours.

cards.title: Read the Viewpoint Plaque
cards.subtitle: State College Boulevard — mapped skyline viewpoint
cards.notes: Head north on State College Boulevard and use the brass plaque to identify the peaks and Los Angeles skyline.
cards.short_summary: A compact overlook with a labeled panorama of regional landmarks.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Mountain View Park at 2601 N. State College Boulevard and says its central viewpoint has a brass plaque identifying surrounding landmarks.
cards.source_title: Mountain View Park | List of Parks | Fullerton, CA
cards.access_notes: The official page lists parking, picnic tables, and a viewpoint but does not state operating hours.

cards.title: Walk the Hilly Park Loop
cards.subtitle: Rolling Hills Drive — walking and hiking trails
cards.notes: Approach the park from the Rolling Hills Drive side and follow designated walkways or natural-surface hiking trails.
cards.short_summary: A large regional park block with a documented network of walking routes.
cards.evidence_claim: OC Parks documents bicycle and hiking or walking trails at Ted Craig Regional Park, located at 3300 State College Boulevard.
cards.source_title: Ted Craig Regional Park | OC Parks
cards.access_notes: Open daily 7:00 a.m.–9:00 p.m. in spring and summer and 7:00 a.m.–6:00 p.m. in fall and winter; vehicle parking fees apply.

cards.title: Circle the Lake on Dirt Trails
cards.subtitle: Lakeview Drive — lakeside recreation trail
cards.notes: Follow Lakeview Drive to Laguna Lake Park and take the hard-packed dirt trail around the water for an outdoor reset.
cards.short_summary: A lakeside corridor stop built around an unpaved walking circuit.
cards.evidence_claim: The City places Laguna Lake Park at 3120 Lakeview Drive and documents hard-packed dirt trails around the lake.
cards.source_title: Laguna Lake Park | List of Parks | Fullerton, CA
cards.access_notes: A California fishing license is required for anglers age 16 and older; the official page does not state park hours.

cards.title: Climb the Pine Forest Stairs
cards.subtitle: Harbor Boulevard — historic park stairway
cards.notes: Travel along Harbor Boulevard to Hillcrest Park and use the Pine Forest Stairs as the block’s focused activity.
cards.short_summary: A mature, shaded park distinguished by its stone stairways.
cards.evidence_claim: The City lists Hillcrest Park at 1200 N. Harbor Boulevard and includes the Pine Forest Stairs among its amenities.
cards.source_title: Hillcrest Park | Facility Directory | Fullerton, CA
cards.access_notes: Observe posted one-way directions or other current instructions on the staircases.

cards.title: Pause Under the Shade Trees
cards.subtitle: Wilshire Avenue — shaded plaza seating
cards.notes: Turn onto East Wilshire Avenue and claim a shaded seat in the plaza before exploring the surrounding civic blocks.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped downtown pause point with seating and an interactive fountain.
cards.evidence_claim: The City locates Fullerton Downtown Plaza at 125 E. Wilshire Avenue and lists shaded seating and an interactive fountain among its amenities.
cards.source_title: Downtown Plaza | List of Parks | Fullerton, CA
cards.access_notes: The plaza page does not state operating hours; events may affect access to portions of the space.

cards.title: Settle In for a Library Session
cards.subtitle: Commonwealth Avenue — public library
cards.notes: Use Commonwealth Avenue to reach the Main Library, then plan a reading or research session within posted hours.
cards.short_summary: A civic study destination on the Commonwealth Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Fullerton Public Library lists its Main Library at 353 W. Commonwealth Avenue and publishes current weekly public hours.
cards.source_title: Locations and Hours | Fullerton Public Library
cards.access_notes: Listed hours are Tuesday–Thursday 11:00 a.m.–7:00 p.m. and Friday–Saturday 11:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; closed Sunday and Monday.

cards.title: Make the Station Your Transit Link
cards.subtitle: Santa Fe Avenue — regional rail station
cards.notes: Follow Santa Fe Avenue to the station and use the posted platform and parking information to plan a regional trip.
cards.short_summary: A clearly marked rail gateway from Fullerton’s Santa Fe Avenue corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Metrolink’s official station page identifies Fullerton Station on Santa Fe Avenue and provides station parking information.
cards.access_notes: Check the official station page and current train schedule before travel; train fare is required for rail service.
